---
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/modules/master/modules/environment-schema.json
channels:
  - conda-forge
  - bioconda
dependencies:
  - bioconda::bioconductor-metaproviz=4.99.0

process METAPROVIZ_INTERNALSTANDARD {
    tag "$meta.id"
    label 'process_single'

    conda "${moduleDir}/environment.yml"
    container "${ workflow.containerEngine in ['singularity', 'apptainer'] && !task.ext.singularity_pull_docker_container ?
        'https://depot.galaxyproject.org/singularity/bioconductor-metaproviz:4.99.0--r45hdfd78af_0' :
        'quay.io/biocontainers/bioconductor-metaproviz:4.99.0--r45hdfd78af_0' }"

    input:
    tuple val(meta), path(se_rds), path(data_matrix), path(feature_matrix), path(sample_matrix)
    val output_format

    output:
    tuple val(meta), path("*.is_filtered.rds")                , optional: true, emit: se
    tuple val(meta), path("*.is_filtered.*_matrix.{tsv,csv}") , optional: true, emit: filtered_matrices
    tuple val(meta), path("*.cv.tsv")                         , emit: cv_table
    tuple val(meta), path("*.condition_cv.tsv")               , emit: condition_cv
    tuple val(meta), path("*.plots.rds")                      , emit: plots
    tuple val(meta), path("*.report.html")                    , emit: report
    tuple val(meta), path("*.log")                            , emit: log
    tuple val("${task.process}"), val('metaproviz'), val('4.99.0'), emit: versions_metaproviz, topic: versions
    tuple val("${task.process}"), val('r-base'), val('4.5.3'), emit: versions_r_base, topic: versions

    when:
    task.ext.when == null || task.ext.when

    script:
    template 'metaproviz_internalstandard.R'

    stub:
    def prefix  = task.ext.prefix ?: "${meta.id}"
    """
    touch ${prefix}.is_filtered.rds ${prefix}.cv.tsv \\
          ${prefix}.is_filtered.{data_matrix,feature_matrix,sample_matrix}.tsv \\
          ${prefix}.condition_cv.tsv ${prefix}.plots.rds \\
          ${prefix}.report.html ${prefix}.log
    """
}

---
name: "nf-core/metaproviz/internalstandard"
description: "Quality-control check on internal standard (IS) spike-in features. Their\
  \ coefficient of variation (CV) across the samples shows the technical noise of\
  \ the measurement, overall and per condition. The IS are removed from the output\
  \ data."
keywords:
- "metabolomics"
- "quality control"
- "internal standard"
- "coefficient of variation"
- "MetaProViz"
tools:
- metaproviz:
    description: "MetaProViz — Metabolomics Processing, functional analysis and Visualization."
    homepage: "https://saezlab.github.io/MetaProViz/"
    documentation: "https://saezlab.github.io/MetaProViz/"
    tool_dev_url: "https://github.com/saezlab/MetaProViz"
    doi: "10.1038/s44320-026-00231-8"
    licence:
    - "BSD-3-Clause"
    identifier: ""
input:
- - meta:
      type: "map"
      description: "Groovy Map containing sample information\ne.g. `[ id:'test' ]`\n"
  - se_rds:
      type: "file"
      description: "A SummarizedExperiment saved as RDS. The assay holds the numerical\
        \ values of the metabolites, the rowData the feature metadata and the colData\
        \ the sample metadata. Both NA and 0 count as not detected. The data must\
        \ not contain pool or QC samples. Use either this input or the three inputs\
        \ data_matrix, feature_matrix and sample_matrix, not both."
      pattern: "*.rds"
      optional: true
      ontologies: []
  - data_matrix:
      type: "file"
      description: "Numerical values of the metabolites as TSV or CSV file, with the\
        \ features in rows and the samples in columns. The first column holds the\
        \ feature IDs. Empty cells, NA and 0 count as not detected. Required together\
        \ with feature_matrix and sample_matrix."
      pattern: "*.{tsv,csv}"
      optional: true
      ontologies:
      - edam: "http://edamontology.org/format_3475"
      - edam: "http://edamontology.org/format_3752"
  - feature_matrix:
      type: "file"
      description: "Feature metadata as TSV or CSV file. The first column holds the\
        \ feature IDs, matching the rows of data_matrix. Required together with data_matrix\
        \ and sample_matrix."
      pattern: "*.{tsv,csv}"
      optional: true
      ontologies:
      - edam: "http://edamontology.org/format_3475"
      - edam: "http://edamontology.org/format_3752"
  - sample_matrix:
      type: "file"
      description: "Sample metadata as TSV or CSV file. The first column holds the\
        \ sample IDs, matching the columns of data_matrix. The data must not contain\
        \ pool or QC samples. Required together with data_matrix and feature_matrix."
      pattern: "*.{tsv,csv}"
      optional: true
      ontologies:
      - edam: "http://edamontology.org/format_3475"
      - edam: "http://edamontology.org/format_3752"
- output_format:
    type: "string"
    description: "Format of the output without the internal standards (IS). `se` (or\
      \ an empty value) writes the SummarizedExperiment as RDS, `tsv` or `csv` write\
      \ it as three tables (data_matrix, feature_matrix and sample_matrix)."
output:
  se:
  - - meta:
        type: "map"
        description: "Groovy Map containing sample information\ne.g. `[ id:'test'\
          \ ]`\n"
    - '*.is_filtered.rds':
        type: "file"
        description: "SummarizedExperiment without the internal standards (IS), written\
          \ if output_format is `se` or empty."
        pattern: "*.is_filtered.rds"
        optional: true
        ontologies: []
  filtered_matrices:
  - - meta:
        type: "map"
        description: "Groovy Map containing sample information\ne.g. `[ id:'test'\
          \ ]`\n"
    - '*.is_filtered.*_matrix.{tsv,csv}':
        type: "file"
        description: "Data without the IS as data_matrix, feature_matrix and sample_matrix\
          \ tables, written if output_format is `tsv` or `csv`."
        pattern: "*.is_filtered.*_matrix.{tsv,csv}"
        optional: true
        ontologies:
        - edam: "http://edamontology.org/format_3475"
        - edam: "http://edamontology.org/format_3752"
  cv_table:
  - - meta:
        type: "map"
        description: "Groovy Map containing sample information\ne.g. `[ id:'test'\
          \ ]`\n"
    - '*.cv.tsv':
        type: "file"
        description: "Table with one row per IS and the columns CV, HighVar and MissingValuepercentage.\
          \ The CV is given in percent."
        pattern: "*.cv.tsv"
        ontologies:
        - edam: "http://edamontology.org/format_3475"
  condition_cv:
  - - meta:
        type: "map"
        description: "Groovy Map containing sample information\ne.g. `[ id:'test'\
          \ ]`\n"
    - '*.condition_cv.tsv':
        type: "file"
        description: "Table with one row per IS and one column per condition, holding\
          \ the CV in percent."
        pattern: "*.condition_cv.tsv"
        ontologies:
        - edam: "http://edamontology.org/format_3475"
  plots:
  - - meta:
        type: "map"
        description: "Groovy Map containing sample information\ne.g. `[ id:'test'\
          \ ]`\n"
    - '*.plots.rds':
        type: "file"
        description: "ggplot objects, one box plot per IS and the PCA, CV histogram\
          \ and CV violin plots of MetaProViz."
        pattern: "*.plots.rds"
        ontologies: []
  report:
  - - meta:
        type: "map"
        description: "Groovy Map containing sample information\ne.g. `[ id:'test'\
          \ ]`\n"
    - '*.report.html':
        type: "file"
        description: "HTML report with the run summary, the CV tables, the box plots\
          \ and a section on IS that have no usable CV."
        pattern: "*.report.html"
        ontologies:
        - edam: "http://edamontology.org/format_2331"
  log:
  - - meta:
        type: "map"
        description: "Groovy Map containing sample information\ne.g. `[ id:'test'\
          \ ]`\n"
    - '*.log':
        type: "file"
        description: "INFO/WARN log."
        pattern: "*.log"
        ontologies: []
  versions_metaproviz:
  - - ${task.process}:
        type: "string"
        description: "The name of the process"
    - metaproviz:
        type: "string"
        description: "The name of the tool"
    - "4.99.0":
        type: "string"
        description: "The version of MetaProViz"
  versions_r_base:
  - - ${task.process}:
        type: "string"
        description: "The name of the process"
    - r-base:
        type: "string"
        description: "The name of the tool"
    - "4.5.3":
        type: "string"
        description: "The version of base R"
topics:
  versions:
  - - ${task.process}:
        type: "string"
        description: "The name of the process"
    - metaproviz:
        type: "string"
        description: "The name of the tool"
    - "4.99.0":
        type: "string"
        description: "The version of MetaProViz"
  - - ${task.process}:
        type: "string"
        description: "The name of the process"
    - r-base:
        type: "string"
        description: "The name of the tool"
    - "4.5.3":
        type: "string"
        description: "The version of base R"
authors:
- "@christinaschmidt1"
- "@giuliaroeth"
maintainers:
- "@christinaschmidt1"
- "@giuliaroeth"
version: "0.0.0-5eae6c7"
license: "MIT License"

#!/usr/bin/env Rscript # ============================================================================= # metaproviz_internalstandard.R — technical-QC check on the internal-standard spike-ins # # Approach: re-use MetaProViz::pool_estimation on the SE subsetted to just the # IS features, with every sample flagged as "Pool" (because for IS we want the # CV across all samples — IS should be constant, so a high CV reveals # technical issues, not biology). # # Picking the IS features (top precedence first): # 1. --internal_standards valine-d8,hippuric acid-d5,... (explicit list) # 2. --pattern "regex" (user regex) # 3. Default auto-detect on the common IS naming conventions: # -dN suffix (deuterated, e.g. valine-d8) # -13CN suffix (carbon-13 labelled) # ISTD anywhere # IS_ prefix / _IS suffix / bare 'IS' # # The CV is computed across all samples of the input. Pool/QC samples must be removed before this module (for example # with the metaproviz/poolestimation module), they are not detected here and would be used like all other samples. # # The IS are removed from the SE, which is written as .is_filtered.rds. The removed IS are the rows of # .cv.tsv (one row per IS, with the CV and the HighVar flag), their values are in the input data. # # No hard stop when the IS have no usable values (all not detected, one value only, identical values): the report and # the log say which of these cases applies. The module stops only if no IS is found or if every feature is an IS. # ============================================================================= set.seed(42) suppressPackageStartupMessages({ library(dplyr); library(tidyr); library(tibble); library(magrittr) library(ggplot2); library(SummarizedExperiment); library(S4Vectors) }) suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(MetaProViz)) # ── PARSE PARAMETERS FROM NEXTFLOW ────────────────────────────────────────── nullify <- function(x) if (is.null(x) || x == "" || x == "null" || x == "[]") NULL else x # Options in list_opts hold a comma-separated list. Their value is everything after the option name, split at the # commas, so names with spaces need no quoting. A name with a comma goes in double quotes. parse_args <- function(x, list_opts = character(0)) { if (is.null(x) || !nzchar(trimws(x))) return(list()) args_list <- unlist(strsplit(x, ' ?--')[[1]])[-1] parsed <- list() for (a in args_list) { nm <- scan(text = a, what = 'character', quiet = TRUE, nmax = 1) if (length(nm) == 0) next if (nm %in% list_opts) { rest <- trimws(sub("^[^[:space:]]+", "", a)) parsed[[nm]] <- scan(text = rest, what = 'character', sep = ",", quote = '"', strip.white = TRUE, quiet = TRUE) } else { z <- scan(text = a, what = 'character', quiet = TRUE) length(z) <- 2 if (!is.na(z[2])) parsed[[z[1]]] <- z[2] } } parsed } opt <- list( internal_standards = character(0), pattern = "", cutoff_cv = "30", conditions_col = "Conditions", id_columns = character(0) ) # R raw string: quotes and apostrophes inside the arguments (feature names like 5'-AMP) cannot break the R code. args_opt <- parse_args(r"---($task.ext.args)---", list_opts = c("internal_standards", "id_columns")) for (ao in names(args_opt)) { if (!ao %in% names(opt)) stop(paste("Invalid option:", ao)) opt[[ao]] <- args_opt[[ao]] } se_path <- nullify('$se_rds') data_matrix_path <- nullify('$data_matrix') feature_matrix_path <- nullify('$feature_matrix') sample_matrix_path <- nullify('$sample_matrix') internal_standards_list <- opt\$internal_standards is_list_str <- paste(internal_standards_list, collapse = ",") user_pattern <- opt\$pattern cutoff_cv <- as.numeric(opt\$cutoff_cv) # colData column holding experimental condition, used to break the IS CV out # per condition (condition_cv output). Column not found => condition_cv is # written header-only. conditions_col <- opt\$conditions_col id_columns_list <- opt\$id_columns id_columns_str <- paste(id_columns_list, collapse = ",") prefix <- ifelse('$task.ext.prefix' == 'null', '$meta.id', '$task.ext.prefix') # output_format is a val input of the module. # se (or an empty value): the SE without the IS as one RDS. tsv/csv: three files (data, feature and sample matrix), the same shape as the # input matrices. output_format_in <- trimws('$output_format') output_format <- if (output_format_in %in% c("", "null", "[]")) "se" else tolower(output_format_in) out_files <- function(base) if (output_format == "se") paste0(base, ".rds") else paste0(base, c(".data_matrix.", ".feature_matrix.", ".sample_matrix."), output_format) se_out <- out_files(paste0(prefix, ".is_filtered")) cv_out <- paste0(prefix, ".cv.tsv") condition_cv_out <- paste0(prefix, ".condition_cv.tsv") plots_out <- paste0(prefix, ".plots.rds") report_out <- paste0(prefix, ".report.html") log_out <- paste0(prefix, ".log") # Default regex — case-insensitive PCRE. Covers common IS labels. DEFAULT_PATTERN <- "-d\\\\d+|-13C\\\\d*|ISTD|^IS_|_IS\$|^IS\$" # Feature metadata columns that hold database IDs or annotations such as pathways (found by name, or set with # --id_columns). ID_PATTERN <- "hmdb|kegg|chebi|pubchem|inchi|smiles|lipidmaps|swisslipids|metacyc|biocyc|chembl|drugbank|pathway|(^|[._ -])cas([._ -]|\$)" # ── LOGGING ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── ll <- character(0); wc <- 0; ec <- 0 log_msg <- function(lev = "INFO", ...) { txt <- paste0("[", lev, "] ", paste(..., sep = "")) ll <<- c(ll, txt); message(txt) if (lev == "WARN") wc <<- wc + 1 if (lev == "ERROR") ec <<- ec + 1 } log_section <- function(t) { sep <- paste(rep("─", 60), collapse = "") ll <<- c(ll, "", sep, paste0(" ", t), sep) message(sep, "\\n ", t, "\\n", sep) } flush_log <- function(p = log_out) { writeLines(c(ll, "", sprintf("SUMMARY: %d warning(s), %d error(s)", wc, ec)), p) } abort <- function(...) { log_msg("ERROR", ...); flush_log(); stop(paste0(...), call. = FALSE) } if (!output_format %in% c("se", "tsv", "csv")) abort("output_format must be se, tsv or csv (empty means se), not '", output_format_in, "'.") esc <- function(x) gsub(">", ">", gsub("<", "<", gsub("&", "&", x, fixed = TRUE), fixed = TRUE), fixed = TRUE) # Names for the report: at most 25, and a pointer to the log file only if not all of them are shown. names_html <- function(x, max_n = 25) paste0( paste0("", esc(head(x, max_n)), "", collapse = " "), if (length(x) > max_n) paste0(" and ", length(x) - max_n, " more (see ", esc(log_out), ")") else "") # IS names with a detail in brackets (the value and the sample), at most 25 shown. info_html <- function(ids, info, max_n = 25) paste0( paste0("", esc(head(ids, max_n)), " (", esc(head(info, max_n)), ")", collapse = ", "), if (length(ids) > max_n) paste0(" and ", length(ids) - max_n, " more (see ", esc(log_out), ")") else "") # ── LOAD SE ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── log_section("Loading input data") # Two acceptable input shapes, mutually exclusive: --se (a SummarizedExperiment # .rds), or all three of --data_matrix/--feature_matrix/--sample_matrix (plain # TSV/CSV, language-independent). Test data is provided in both shapes; this # module accepts either so users aren't forced into one or the other. have_se <- !is.null(se_path) && nzchar(se_path) have_csv <- !is.null(data_matrix_path) && nzchar(data_matrix_path) && !is.null(feature_matrix_path) && nzchar(feature_matrix_path) && !is.null(sample_matrix_path) && nzchar(sample_matrix_path) have_partial_csv <- !have_csv && ( (!is.null(data_matrix_path) && nzchar(data_matrix_path)) || (!is.null(feature_matrix_path) && nzchar(feature_matrix_path)) || (!is.null(sample_matrix_path) && nzchar(sample_matrix_path)) ) if (have_se && have_csv) abort("Provide either --se, or all three of --data_matrix/--feature_matrix/", "--sample_matrix, not both.") if (have_se && have_partial_csv) abort("--se was provided together with some of --data_matrix/--feature_matrix/", "--sample_matrix; provide either --se alone, or all three of those, not a mix.") if (have_partial_csv) abort("--data_matrix, --feature_matrix, and --sample_matrix must all be ", "provided together.") if (!have_se && !have_csv) abort("Provide either --se , or all three of --data_matrix/", "--feature_matrix/--sample_matrix.") if (have_se) { if (!file.exists(se_path)) abort("SE file not found: ", se_path) se <- readRDS(se_path) if (!is(se, "SummarizedExperiment")) abort("Object is not a SummarizedExperiment.") log_msg("INFO", "Loaded SE from ", basename(se_path), ": ", nrow(se), " features × ", ncol(se), " samples.") } else { for (p in c(data_matrix_path, feature_matrix_path, sample_matrix_path)) if (!file.exists(p)) abort("Input file not found: ", p) read_flat <- function(path) { sep <- if (grepl("\\\\.csv\$", path, ignore.case = TRUE)) "," else "\\t" tryCatch(read.delim(path, sep = sep, check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE), error = function(e) abort("Failed to read ", path, ": ", conditionMessage(e))) } dm <- read_flat(data_matrix_path) fm <- read_flat(feature_matrix_path) sm <- read_flat(sample_matrix_path) if (ncol(dm) < 2) abort("--data_matrix must have a feature-ID column plus at least one ", "sample column.") feature_ids <- as.character(dm[[1]]) assay_matrix <- as.matrix(dm[, -1, drop = FALSE]) rownames(assay_matrix) <- feature_ids mode(assay_matrix) <- "numeric" sample_ids <- as.character(sm[[1]]) col_data <- sm[, -1, drop = FALSE] rownames(col_data) <- sample_ids feature_ids2 <- as.character(fm[[1]]) row_data <- fm[, -1, drop = FALSE] rownames(row_data) <- feature_ids2 missing_samples <- setdiff(colnames(assay_matrix), sample_ids) if (length(missing_samples) > 0) abort("--data_matrix has sample column(s) not present in ", "--sample_matrix: ", paste(missing_samples, collapse = ", ")) missing_features <- setdiff(rownames(assay_matrix), feature_ids2) if (length(missing_features) > 0) abort("--data_matrix has feature(s) not present in --feature_matrix: ", paste(head(missing_features, 5), collapse = ", "), if (length(missing_features) > 5) ", ..." else "") col_data <- col_data[colnames(assay_matrix), , drop = FALSE] row_data <- row_data[rownames(assay_matrix), , drop = FALSE] se <- SummarizedExperiment(assays = list(counts = assay_matrix), colData = col_data, rowData = row_data) log_msg("INFO", "Built SE from data_matrix/feature_matrix/sample_matrix: ", nrow(se), " features × ", ncol(se), " samples.") } source_label <- if (have_se) { basename(se_path) } else { paste(basename(data_matrix_path), basename(feature_matrix_path), basename(sample_matrix_path), sep = " + ") } n_samples_input <- ncol(se) # ── IDENTIFY IS FEATURES ──────────────────────────────────────────────────── log_section("Identifying internal-standard features") feat_names <- rownames(se) is_feats <- character(0) strategy <- "none" is_attempted <- character(0) # ways of finding the IS that were tried and found no feature # 1) Explicit list if (nzchar(is_list_str)) { asked <- trimws(internal_standards_list) asked <- asked[nzchar(asked)] is_feats <- intersect(asked, feat_names) missing <- setdiff(asked, feat_names) if (length(missing) > 0) log_msg("WARN", "Requested IS feature(s) not found in SE: ", paste(missing, collapse = ", ")) strategy <- "explicit_list" if (length(is_feats) == 0) is_attempted <- c(is_attempted, list = "explicit list (--internal_standards)") } # 2) User pattern if (length(is_feats) == 0 && nzchar(user_pattern)) { hit <- grepl(user_pattern, feat_names, ignore.case = TRUE, perl = TRUE) is_feats <- feat_names[hit] strategy <- "user_pattern" if (length(is_feats) == 0) is_attempted <- c(is_attempted, pattern = sprintf("pattern '%s' (--pattern)", user_pattern)) } # 3) Default pattern id_status <- "not run" id_cols <- character(0) id_flagged <- character(0) if (length(is_feats) == 0) { hit <- grepl(DEFAULT_PATTERN, feat_names, ignore.case = TRUE, perl = TRUE) is_feats <- feat_names[hit] strategy <- "default" # A name can look like a standard but belong to a real metabolite (Vitamin-D3 matches -d3). A real metabolite # usually has an entry in a database, a spike-in standard usually has none. So a feature found by the default pattern # that has a database ID in the feature metadata is flagged in the log and the report, but still used as IS. Only the # presence of an ID counts, a missing ID proves nothing. Names given with --internal_standards or --pattern are never # checked. if (length(is_feats) > 0) { feat_info <- as.data.frame(rowData(se), check.names = FALSE) id_cols <- if (nzchar(id_columns_str)) trimws(id_columns_list) else grep(ID_PATTERN, colnames(feat_info), ignore.case = TRUE, value = TRUE) id_cols <- intersect(id_cols, colnames(feat_info)) has_id <- function(x) { v <- trimws(iconv(as.character(x), "UTF-8", "UTF-8", sub = "")) # invalid characters would stop trimws() !is.na(v) & !(toupper(v) %in% c("", "NA", "NAN", "N/A", "-")) } if (length(id_cols) == 0) { id_status <- "no_columns" } else if (!any(vapply(id_cols, function(cn) any(has_id(feat_info[[cn]])), logical(1)))) { id_status <- "empty" } else { id_status <- "checked" id_matrix <- do.call(cbind, lapply(id_cols, function(cn) has_id(feat_info[is_feats, cn]))) dimnames(id_matrix) <- list(is_feats, id_cols) id_flagged <- is_feats[rowSums(id_matrix) > 0] # for each flagged name, the columns in which an ID was found id_found_cols <- lapply(setNames(id_flagged, id_flagged), function(f) id_cols[id_matrix[f, ]]) } } if (id_status == "checked" && length(id_flagged) > 0) { log_msg("WARN", "Names with an entry in the database ID columns of the feature metadata: ", paste0(id_flagged, " (", vapply(id_found_cols, paste, character(1), collapse = ", "), ")", collapse = ", "), ". They are used as IS. Please check that they are real IS.") } else if (id_status == "checked") { log_msg("INFO", "Checked the names found by the default pattern against the feature metadata columns with database ", "IDs: ", paste(id_cols, collapse = ", "), ". None of the names has an entry in these columns. ", if (nzchar(id_columns_str)) "The columns were given with --id_columns." else "The columns were selected by default, --id_columns sets them directly.") } else if (id_status == "no_columns") { log_msg("INFO", "The feature metadata has no columns with database IDs, and the names found by the default pattern ", "could not be checked. Columns are recognised by names such as HMDB, KEGG or ChEBI, --id_columns sets them ", "directly.") } else if (id_status == "empty") { log_msg("INFO", "The feature metadata columns with database IDs (", paste(id_cols, collapse = ", "), ") are empty, and the names found by the default pattern could not be checked.") } } # Wording of the detection for the log and the report is_label <- switch(strategy, explicit_list = "explicit list (--internal_standards)", user_pattern = sprintf("pattern '%s' (--pattern)", user_pattern), "default naming conventions") is_label_html <- switch(strategy, explicit_list = "explicit list --internal_standards", user_pattern = sprintf("pattern --pattern %s", esc(user_pattern)), "default naming conventions: deuterated -dN, 13C, ISTD, IS_ prefix, _IS suffix") is_attempted_txt <- paste(is_attempted, collapse = " and the ") is_attempted_html <- paste(vapply(names(is_attempted), function(k) if (k == "list") { "explicit list --internal_standards" } else sprintf("pattern --pattern %s", esc(user_pattern)), character(1)), collapse = " and the ") if (length(is_attempted) > 0 && strategy == "default" && length(is_feats) > 0) log_msg("WARN", "No IS features were found by the ", is_attempted_txt, ". The IS detection falls back to the default naming conventions.") if (length(is_feats) == 0) { ways <- c(is_attempted, "default naming conventions") ways_txt <- if (length(ways) == 1) ways else paste0(paste(head(ways, -1), collapse = ", the "), " and the ", tail(ways, 1)) abort("No IS features were found by the ", ways_txt, ". This report evaluates IS (spike-in) features to assess the technical noise of the measurement, independent of biology. IS are added in a fixed, known amount to every sample before measurement. Unlike real metabolites, their values are expected to stay constant across the run.

This module computes the coefficient of variation (CV) of each IS across all samples. Pool and QC samples must be removed before this module (e.g. with metaproviz/poolestimation), since their already-pooled nature would understate the true injection-to-injection variability. A high CV indicates instrument drift or injection issues rather than biological variation.

CV is calculated as:

CV(%%) = 100 × sd(x1, x2, ..., xn) / mean(x1, x2, ..., xn)

MetaProViz::pool_estimation() uses the same formula, so this module reuses that function. The function is made for pool samples, which are aliquots of the same mixture that are measured several times. A feature should have the same value in all of them. An IS is added in the same amount to all samples and should therefore give the same value in each sample. For this reason all samples are temporarily labelled as pool samples for the calculation. In some cases the function cannot be used (a single IS, or an IS with identical values in every sample). Then the module calculates the CV directly with the formula. An IS with no value or only one value has no CV and is listed under "IS to check".

If condition metadata is available, the same CV calculation is additionally broken down per condition (see the "CV per IS, per condition" table further down), and the box plots below also color individual dots by condition.

%s

Plots

Each IS gets one box plot below, generated with MetaProViz\\'s viz_superplot() function, showing its values across all samples used for the CV calculation.

What to expect: dots of different colors should be interspersed throughout the box, not clustered by color, since the IS is expected to behave the same regardless of condition. If dots of one color cluster together at their own distinct position, that points to a systematic shift for that specific condition (e.g. a batch effect). Without condition metadata, all dots are shown in black instead.

CV per IS, overall

The CV of every IS, calculated across all samples together. The table has one row per IS. CV is given in percent. HighVar shows whether the CV is above the cutoff of %s%%. MissingValuepercentage is the percentage of samples in which the IS was not detected, which means that its value is missing or 0. The table is saved as %s.
